"'''Blurry'''" is a song by the American rock band [[Puddle of Mudd]]. It was released on October 16, 2001, as the second single from the band's debut album ''[[Come Clean (Puddle of Mudd album)|Come Clean]]'' (2001). It was 2002's most successful rock song in the United States, topping the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Mainstream Rock]] and [[Modern Rock Tracks]] charts as well as their year-end listings. "Blurry" also found success outside the US, reaching the top 20 in Ireland, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. In 2024, the staff of ''[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]'' included the song in their list of "50 Kick-Butt Post-Grunge Songs We Can Get Behind".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://consequence.net/list/best-post-grunge-songs/fuel-shimmer/|title=50 Kick-Butt Post-Grunge Songs We Can Get Behind|magazine=[[Consequence (website)|Consequence]]|date=May 20, 2024|access-date=September 23, 2026}}</ref>

"Blurry" is a song by the American rock band Puddle of Mudd. It was released on October 16, 2001, as the second single from the band's debut album Come Clean (2001). It was 2002's most successful rock song in the United States, topping the Billboard Mainstream Rock and Modern Rock Tracks charts as well as their year-end listings. "Blurry" also found success outside the US, reaching the top 20 in Ireland, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. In 2024, the staff of Consequence included the song in their list of "50 Kick-Butt Post-Grunge Songs We Can Get Behind".

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
Puddle of Mudd played small shows in the Kansas City area for most of the 1990s with little mainstream success.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://returnofrock.com/puddle-of-mudd-albums-ranked/|title=Puddle of Mudd Albums Ranked |website= Return of Rock|date=June 4, 2020 |accessdate=December 21, 2022}}</ref> However, singer Wes Scantlin got a demo tape to [[Limp Bizkit]] singer [[Fred Durst]] when Limp Bizkit were in town on October 12, 1999, on the [[Family Values Tour 1999|Family Values Tour]], and Durst's label [[Flawless Records]] signed him to a recording contract. Unimpressed with Scantlin's bandmates, Flawless Records scrapped them all,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/limp-bizkit-136-1389655|title=Flawless Stuff from Fred |website= [[NME]]|date=May 16, 2001 |accessdate=December 25, 2022}}</ref> rebuilt the group with musicians Scantlin had never seen before, and flew him out to Los Angeles in late 2000 to record with them. He spent his days fiddling with his acoustic guitar in a hotel room on [[Hollywood Boulevard]], where he reworked a previous Puddle of Mudd song called "Electron Moon" into "Blurry".<ref name="song">{{cite web|url=https://americansongwriter.com/behind-the-song-blurry-by-puddle-of-mudd/|title=Behind the Song : "Blurry" by Puddle of Mudd |last=Bennett|first=Macie|website=American Songwriter|date=February 17, 2021 |accessdate=December 21, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/wes-scantlin-puddle-of-mudd|title=Wes Scantlin of Puddle of Mudd : Songwriter Interviews |last=Prato|first=Greg|website= Songfacts|date=December 19, 2022 |accessdate=December 21, 2022}}</ref>

“’Blurry’ was basically about being flown to freaking Los Angeles and y’know, I didn't have any friends so they had put me into a hotel room,” Scantlin told ''American Songwriter''. “I didn't know anybody at all. And I was just missing my family and son, I missed my grandma and stuff.”<ref name="song" />
sections.text:
Puddle of Mudd played small shows in the Kansas City area for most of the 1990s with little mainstream success. However, singer Wes Scantlin got a demo tape to Limp Bizkit singer Fred Durst when Limp Bizkit were in town on October 12, 1999, on the Family Values Tour, and Durst's label Flawless Records signed him to a recording contract. Unimpressed with Scantlin's bandmates, Flawless Records scrapped them all, rebuilt the group with musicians Scantlin had never seen before, and flew him out to Los Angeles in late 2000 to record with them. He spent his days fiddling with his acoustic guitar in a hotel room on Hollywood Boulevard, where he reworked a previous Puddle of Mudd song called "Electron Moon" into "Blurry".

“’Blurry’ was basically about being flown to freaking Los Angeles and y’know, I didn't have any friends so they had put me into a hotel room,” Scantlin told American Songwriter. “I didn't know anybody at all. And I was just missing my family and son, I missed my grandma and stuff.”

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Blurry" is a [[post-grunge]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://consequence.net/aux-out/in-defense-of-post-grunge-music/ |title=In Defense of Post-Grunge Music |work=[[Consequence of Sound]] |last=Geffen |first=Sasha |date=October 7, 2013 |access-date=September 21, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://consequence.net/list/best-post-grunge-songs/|title=50 Best Post-Grunge Songs|last=Graves|first=Wren|website=[[Consequence (publication)|Consequence]]|date=May 20, 2024|access-date=April 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|URL=https://numetalagenda.com/feature/the-15-greatest-and-10-worst-post-grunge-songs-of-all-time/|title=The 15 Greatest (and 10 Worst) Post-Grunge Songs of All Time|date=April 11, 2024|website=Nu Metal Agenda|access-date=December 26, 2025}}</ref> and [[alternative rock]]<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://consequence.net/2017/07/ranking-every-alternative-rock-hit-from-worst-to-best/5/|title=Ranking: Every Alternative Rock No. 1 Hit from Worst to Best|last=Cosores|first=Philip|magazine=[[Consequence of Sound]]|date=July 4, 2017|access-date=September 3, 2020|page=5}}</ref> song, written in the key of [[E-flat minor|E{{flat}} minor]] with a moderately slow [[tempo]] of 78 beats per minute. The song follows a chord progression of C{{flat}}–D{{flat}}–E{{flat}}m, and the vocals in the song span from D{{flat}}<sub>3</sub> to A{{flat}}<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Blurry|url = http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0042251|website = www.musicnotes.com| date=May 21, 2002 |access-date = January 2, 2016}}</ref>
sections.text: "Blurry" is a post-grunge and alternative rock song, written in the key of E{{flat}} minor with a moderately slow tempo of 78 beats per minute. The song follows a chord progression of C{{flat}}–D{{flat}}–E{{flat}}m, and the vocals in the song span from D{{flat}}<sub>3</sub> to A{{flat}}<sub>4</sub>.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "Blurry" is Puddle of Mudd's most successful song, reaching the number-one spot on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks]] and [[Hot Modern Rock Tracks]] charts for 10 and nine weeks, respectively. This soon propelled the single to mainstream success, reaching the number five spot on both the [[Billboard Hot 100 Airplay|''Billboard'' Hot 100 Airplay]]<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2002-05-25/radio-songs |title=Top 100 Music Hits, Top 100 Music Charts, Top 100 Songs & The Hot 100 |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=August 20, 2011}}</ref> and [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]<ref>[[Joel Whitburn|Whitburn, Joel]] (2004). ''The Billboard Book of Top 40 Hits'', 8th Edition (Billboard Publications), page 510.</ref> and number three on the [[Mainstream Top 40|Pop Songs]] chart. "Blurry" was the eighth-most played song on radio in Canada in 2002.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canoe.com/JamMusicCharts/100_2002.html|title=Top 100 top played radio tracks in Canada in 2002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041123064030/http://www.canoe.com/JamMusicCharts/100_2002.html|access-date=April 11, 2020|archive-date=November 23, 2004}}</ref> The song is also the band's highest selling U.S. single ever, with sales of 753,000 copies, as of 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/60011/chart-watch-extra-top-20-songs-in-digital-history/ |title=Chart Watch Extra: Top 20 Songs In Digital History – Chart Watch |publisher=New.music.yahoo.com |date=August 6, 2010 |access-date=August 20, 2011}}</ref> Additionally, the song's writers, Wes Scantlin, [[Doug Ardito]], and [[Jimmy Allen (musician)|Jimmy Allen]], won [[ASCAP]] (American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers) Song of the Year and Pop Song of the Year for this tune.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ascap.com/playback/2003/fall/popaward.html |title="Elvis Costello Receives Founders Award at 20th Annual Pop Music Awards" American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers Retrieved June 16, 2011 |publisher=Ascap.com |access-date=August 20, 2011}}</ref> "Blurry" also won two ''Billboard'' Awards in 2002, for Modern Rock Track of the Year and Rock Track of the Year. It also received the [[Kerrang! Award for Best Single]]. "Blurry" reached number eight on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on its release there in June 2002, becoming the band's highest-charting single in the United Kingdom.
sections.text: "Blurry" is Puddle of Mudd's most successful song, reaching the number-one spot on the Billboard Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks and Hot Modern Rock Tracks charts for 10 and nine weeks, respectively. This soon propelled the single to mainstream success, reaching the number five spot on both the Billboard Hot 100 Airplay and Billboard Hot 100 and number three on the Pop Songs chart. "Blurry" was the eighth-most played song on radio in Canada in 2002. The song is also the band's highest selling U.S. single ever, with sales of 753,000 copies, as of 2010. Additionally, the song's writers, Wes Scantlin, Doug Ardito, and Jimmy Allen, won ASCAP (American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers) Song of the Year and Pop Song of the Year for this tune. "Blurry" also won two Billboard Awards in 2002, for Modern Rock Track of the Year and Rock Track of the Year. It also received the Kerrang! Award for Best Single. "Blurry" reached number eight on the UK Singles Chart on its release there in June 2002, becoming the band's highest-charting single in the United Kingdom.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The video was directed by [[Limp Bizkit]] vocalist [[Fred Durst]]. The video shows Scantlin playing with his son Jordan, interspersed with shots of the band playing in a garage. Towards the end of the video, a man and a woman (presumably Jordan's mother and stepfather) are shown driving away with Jordan in the back seat as Wes watches sadly.

sections.heading: Covers
sections.wikitext:
* [[P.M. Dawn]] appeared on [[NBC]]'s ''[[Hit Me, Baby, One More Time (TV series)|Hit Me, Baby, One More Time]]'', performing "Set Adrift on Memory Bliss", and covered [[Puddle of Mudd]]'s "Blurry". Despite the fact that Prince Be was still suffering the effects of this stroke, they beat [[Animotion]], [[Missing Persons (band)|Missing Persons]], [[Juice Newton]] and [[Shannon (American singer)|Shannon]] to claim the $20,000 charitable prize, which they contributed to the [[Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation]], as Prince Be was a diabetic. In June 2019, [[P.M. Dawn]] collaborated with musician [[Tommy Marz]] on a studio version of Blurry dedicated to the memory of [[Attrell Cordes]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nationalrockreview.com/artist-news/tommy-marz-drops-new-single-featuring-p-m-dawn/ |title=Tommy Marz Drops New Single Featuring P.M. Dawn |date=June 21, 2019 |access-date=July 1, 2019 |work=[[National Rock Review]] }}</ref>
* On May 21, 2021, [[country rock]] singer-songwriter [[Hardy (singer)|Hardy]] released a cover of "Blurry" with an accompanying music video on YouTube.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cmt.com/news/1834103/hardy-dives-into-his-rock-loving-roots-with-cover-of-puddle-of-mudds-blurry/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522020634/http://www.cmt.com/news/1834103/hardy-dives-into-his-rock-loving-roots-with-cover-of-puddle-of-mudds-blurry/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 22, 2021 |title= HARDY Dives Into His Rock-Loving Roots With Cover Of Puddle Of Mudd's "Blurry" |date=May 21, 2021 |work=[[Country Music Television|CMT]]}}</ref>

* P.M. Dawn appeared on NBC's Hit Me, Baby, One More Time, performing "Set Adrift on Memory Bliss", and covered Puddle of Mudd's "Blurry". Despite the fact that Prince Be was still suffering the effects of this stroke, they beat Animotion, Missing Persons, Juice Newton and Shannon to claim the $20,000 charitable prize, which they contributed to the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation, as Prince Be was a diabetic. In June 2019, P.M. Dawn collaborated with musician Tommy Marz on a studio version of Blurry dedicated to the memory of Attrell Cordes
* On May 21, 2021, country rock singer-songwriter Hardy released a cover of "Blurry" with an accompanying music video on YouTube.

sections.heading: Uses in media
